name: P523 packaging refusal control mutation probe: Linux salvage version-mismatch relabel (release-local.sh)
command: --test 'PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_LOCAL_PATH={} node --test --test-reporter=spec --test-name-pattern="refuses to relabel a different version" papercusp-desktop/test/release-local-linux-reuse.test.js'
summary: Copy-out mutation probe (no in-tree mutation) on the P523 packaging refusal control 'Linux salvage refuses to relabel a different version'. The baseline and the unmutated-copy baseline each ran exactly 1 test and passed. Replacing the version-mismatch branch condition in release-local.sh (the only occurrence) with `if false` let a 0.0.17 salvage be relabelled as the 0.0.18 cut; the refusal test then failed (guard exit 1). The probe reported MUTANT CAUGHT and verified release-local.sh byte-identical afterwards. This proves one of the refusal controls cited by stale counterexample binding 9477; it is not a proof of the other eight controls, and it is preparation evidence, not a full installer build, signing, notarization or P-521 acceptance.

assertions.evidence: Baseline against the tracked file and unmutated-copy baseline against the relocated copy: each 'tests 1, pass 1, fail 0, skipped 0' (node --test spec reporter), exit 0.

Changing `if [[ "$prior_ver" != "$VERSION" ]]; then` to `if false; then` in the Linux/Windows/mac reuse provenance check made 'Linux salvage refuses to relabel a different version' fail: assert.notEqual(result.status, 0) got 0 (ERR_ASSERTION, operator notStrictEqual); guard exit 1.
